history.dynasty: Namgyal dynasty (Sikkimese monarchy); founded by Lhatsun Namkha Jigme, one of the three lamas who crowned Phuntsog Namgyal as the first Chogyal of Sikkim at Norbugang in 1642
history.period: Early 18th century - established 1701; professed to be the first/oldest monastery of Sikkim
history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: the CSV town 'Geyzing' is approximate - Dubdi Monastery stands on a hilltop about 3 km above Yuksom (roughly 35-45 km from Gyalshing town) in Gyalshing district; town corrected to Yuksom. Regarded as the first and oldest monastery of Sikkim, established in 1701 by the ascetic founder Lhatsun Namkha Jigme - one of the three lamas from Tibet who crowned Phuntsog Namgyal as the first Chogyal at Norbugang near Yuksom in 1642 (some secondary sources credit Chogyal Namgyal with its establishment - verify). The name 'Dubdi' means 'the retreat' in the local language, hence 'Hermit's Cell'. A modest two-storey stone structure in Tibetan/Nyingma style with intricately painted interiors and rare preserved manuscripts, surrounded by dense forest including cypress trees said to have been brought from Tibet; it offers views of Mt. Kanchenjunga. It is reached only by an uphill trek of about 3 km (30-60 minutes) from Yuksom, and is part of the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit of Norbugang Chorten, Pemayangtse, Rabdentse ruins, Sanga Choeling, Khecheopalri Lake and Tashiding. COORDINATES FLAG: map.geocode has no Dubdi POI (it resolves only 'Kathok Monastery, Yuksom' about 1 km away, a different monastery); coordinates 27.36662, 88.22985 are from OpenStreetMap/mapcarta (corroborated by aroundus.com, 27.36682, 88.22996). Note Wikipedia's listed Dubdi coordinates (27.067, 88.467) are erroneous - they point to South/East Sikkim, not Yuksom. Religious affiliation verified as Nyingma Tibetan Buddhism - NOT a Hindu temple.

name: Dubdi Monastery
town_description: Yuksom, in Gyalshing district, was the first capital of Sikkim (1642-1670) and the coronation site of the first Chogyal Phuntsog Namgyal at Norbugang in 1642 ('Yuksom' means meeting place of the three learned lamas). It is the gateway to the Dzongri-Goechala trek into Kanchenjunga National Park, about a 5-6 hour drive from Gangtok. Nearby are the Norbugang Chorten and coronation throne, Kathok Lake and Dubdi Monastery.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), approx. 170 km / 5-6 hours (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 150-170 km (verify).
travel.road: Yuksom is reached by road from Gangtok via Jorethang/Legship (about 5-6 hours); the monastery is a 3 km uphill walk (30-60 minutes) from Yuksom through forest - not motorable.

visitor_information.best_time: March to May and October-November for clear weather and trekking season.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Incredible India lists 7:00 AM-4:00 PM (verify); travel sources note the monastery is not always open to the public and only one monk looks after the site.
